title: Tournament Assistant
description: A practical timeline for preparing, running and closing a tournament. Manual checklist, N/A bypasses and automatic checks when data is available.

toolbar.title: Keep the tournament under control
toolbar.description: Scan the current tournament, then tick what is done or mark non-applicable items.

sections.timelineHelp: Before, during and after the tournament. Mandatory items are the backbone; optional items add polish.
sections.scanHelp: Uses the SDK when available. Otherwise the item remains manual.
sections.eventsHelp: PoC buttons for actions that Compet+ will emit as domain events later.

identity.title: Confirm tournament identity
identity.description: Check name, code, dates, place and competition type before publishing anything.
identity.tooltip: Tournament screen → identity block / main information.

responsible.title: Declare the responsible judge
responsible.description: The organizer must know who validates the competition on the day. A sanctioned FFTA competition requires at least one responsible judge, even though Ianseo never blocks anything if it is missing.
responsible.tooltip: Tournament screen → Field team → add the responsible judge (appeal jury, speaker and logistics lead for bigger competitions).

trio.title: Lock local rule / type / sub-rule
trio.description: Pick the local rule, competition type and FFTA sub-rule for good at creation time.
trio.tooltip: Competition screen → New. For a French competition: local rule = French rules, then pick the type (TAE, 2x18m, 2x25m, 18+25m 4 distances, Beursault) and an FFTA sub-rule.
trio.warning: This trio seeds the classes, divisions and rule sets right at creation. Changing it afterwards confuses Ianseo: it recreates classes on top of the existing ones without updating everything. Never touch it once the competition has been created.

code.title: Check the FFTA organizer code
code.description: The "Organized by" field has an organizer code and a name. Only the code really matters.
code.tooltip: Competition screen → Competition information → Organized by. The code must match the 7-digit FFTA club code (region + department + club, e.g. 13 092 for Aix-en-Provence).
code.warning: Ianseo does not validate this at all, only the FFTA side does. A wrong organizer code produces an export file that cannot be matched to the declared event: results cannot be transmitted.

faces.title: Order target faces
faces.description: Order or reserve the right target faces early enough. J-20 is a good safety margin.
faces.tooltip: Use the rule set / distance and target face configuration, then prepare the physical order.

awards.title: Order awards
awards.description: Cups, medals, goodies or vouchers. Optional, but organizers forgetting them become legends for the wrong reason.
awards.tooltip: External logistics for now. Later: Tournament → Logistics.

imported.title: Import the FFTA licensed archer database
imported.description: Mandatory but easy to miss: fetch and import the license file before anyone can be registered properly.
imported.tooltip: Participants → Competitors synchronization → Competitors synchronization. Download parametres_ianseo.ffta (requires an official's access) then run the athlete data synchronization.

refreshed.title: Refresh the archer database before the event
refreshed.description: Re-import the FFTA database right before the competition to catch last-minute club or category changes.
refreshed.tooltip: Participants → Competitors synchronization → Archer database inconsistencies.
refreshed.warning: A fresh import never updates entries that already exist. The inconsistency screen compares both bases, but the FFTA base is all UPPERCASE while Ianseo title-cases entries on registration: expect a lot of false positives. Check the flagged changes by eye instead of trusting the diff alone.

imported.title: Import or create entries
imported.description: The competition must contain archers before field assignment and scorecards make sense.
imported.tooltip: Registrations / Entries → import licenses or create archers manually.

flags.title: Check the Individual shoot / Individual event flags
flags.description: For an archer registered on several sessions, only their first shoot of the day should count in the competition ranking.
flags.tooltip: Registration window → the block of 5 yes/no toggles, bottom right. Switch Individual shoot and Individual event to no on any shoot that is not the archer's first.
flags.warning: All 5 toggles default to yes. An archer added at the last minute on a second session keeps both shoots at yes/yes: at the awards ceremony they show up ranked twice in their category, with nothing in Ianseo warning anyone.

assigned.title: Assign all archers
assigned.description: Every registered archer should have a target and position before printing scorecards.
assigned.tooltip: Field / Target assignment → drag archers to targets or run auto-assignment.
assigned.warning: Shifting target assignments (Participants → Target → move target assignments) is brutal and has no confirmation dialog: a wrong range can stack two archers on the same position, with no undo. Take a backup before any such operation.

installed.title: Install the field
installed.description: Targets, distances, safety layout and waiting line are physically ready.
installed.tooltip: Field plan / printed layout. This is a manual physical check.

scorecards.title: Print scorecards
scorecards.description: Print sheets once target assignment is stable.
scorecards.tooltip: Print / Scorecards or Compet+ field/export actions.

clubs.title: Download club flags/logos
clubs.description: Ianseo can automatically download club flags for registered archers, but only on demand and only for the current competition.
clubs.tooltip: Participants → Competitors synchronization → tick "Country Club logo/flags" then Synchronize athlete data. Re-run it if an archer from a new club is added afterwards.

chronotir.title: Recharge timing devices
chronotir.description: Recharge Chronotir / timing devices and check batteries. Future-you will say thank you.
chronotir.tooltip: Manual equipment check before the event.

backup.title: Create a backup
backup.description: Make a backup before competition day and before big result operations.

faced.title: Set target faces
faced.description: Install the correct target faces on the field before warm-up.
faced.tooltip: Use the field plan and target face configuration.

greffe.title: Prepare the registration desk
greffe.description: Check attendance flow, late entries, labels, payment list and who handles corrections.
greffe.tooltip: Registrations / Greffe workflow. Mostly manual for the PoC.

scored.title: Check scoring flow
scored.description: At least one score is entered and visible. Better to find data flow issues early than during awards.
scored.tooltip: Results or mobile scoring screen → verify entered qualification scores.

live.title: Enable live display
live.description: Optional, but useful for spectators, TV screens and sponsors.

checked.title: Validate rankings
checked.description: Check rankings, ties and obvious score mistakes before announcing results.
checked.tooltip: Results / Rankings → qualification ranking and tie checks.

classement.title: Pick the right ranking printout
classement.description: Distinguish "All results" (ranking by division/class as entered) from "Event ranking" (with FFTA category groupings) before doing the podiums.
classement.tooltip: Print or Qualification → both printouts exist side by side and look alike.
classement.warning: FFTA sometimes merges several age classes into one event (e.g. U21/S1/S2/S3 Men Barebow grouped into a single "Adult Men Barebow" title). Using "All results" then hands out more awards than the rule set allows, with nothing in Ianseo flagging it. Most organizers never notice this distinction.

export.title: Generate the FFTA file
export.description: Generate the federal export after validating final results.
export.tooltip: Export FFTA module → generate the TXT export, to upload at https://extranet.ffta.fr/gsportive/resultats-integrationtxt.html within 48h. A correction is still possible within 10 days; keep the paper scorecards for 1 year.

records.title: Check records
records.description: Look for broken or suspicious records and validate the record workflow if relevant.

archive.title: Archive the competition
archive.description: Final backup, result files, PDF outputs and internal notes are archived.

print.title: Tournament checklist
print.description: Paper version: visible checkboxes, full timeline and useful information for tournament day.

intro: This screen guides you from start to finish. Automatic checks run by themselves; tick the rest as you go, and print the checklist if needed.
